title: Item Embedding
explain: An item embedding encodes each item (document, product, image, user) as a vector so a computer can compare items by geometry instead of by exact words. Items with similar meaning land close together, so 'cheap car' sits near 'affordable automobile'. It is what makes semantic search and recommendations work. (把每个 item 编码成一个向量.)
model:
Two families of vector:

| | Dense | Sparse |
|---|---|---|
| Shape | 64-1,536 floats, all non-zero | one dimension per term, mostly zeros |
| Examples | learned text/image/user embeddings | one-hot, bag-of-words, TF-IDF, BM25 |
| Strength | meaning, paraphrase, cross-language | exact, interpretable, rare tokens (SKUs, error codes) |
| Weakness | opaque dimensions, model-bound | blind to synonyms |

```
offline:  item ──▶ embedding model (vN) ──▶ vector ──▶ index
online :  query ──▶ same model (vN) ──▶ vector ──▶ nearest vectors
```

**Rules that bite**
- **One space:** items and queries must use the same model *and version*; a model upgrade means re-embedding the corpus behind a parallel index.
- **Memory** = `items x dims x bytes`.
- Embed items offline, only the query online.
- **Hybrid** (dense + sparse) often beats either alone.

Next: a [similarity](#/sd/f/similarity) measure and a [similarity search](#/sd/f/similarity-search) index. Exact attributes belong in [user context](#/sd/f/user-context).

details.q: Dense or sparse: how do you decide?
details.a: Dense for meaning: paraphrases ('get my money back' vs 'Refund policy'), synonyms, other languages. Sparse for exact rare tokens such as 'ERR_CONN_4412' or a SKU, where term matching is precise and explainable. Because each fails where the other wins, production search is often hybrid, merging both result lists.

details.q: How much memory do the vectors take?
details.a: `items x dims x bytes`. 10M items x 768 dims x 4 bytes (float32) is about 30.72 GB before index overhead. int8 quantization cuts that 4x to about 7.7 GB, and product quantization 30x or more, each at some recall cost.

details.q: What happens if new documents use embedding model v2 while old ones keep v1 vectors?
details.a: Scores between a v2 query and v1 documents are meaningless: each model learns its own coordinate system, even at the same dimensionality. Nothing errors, so quality silently drops. Build a parallel index with the new model, backfill, then cut over; keep both versions running during the migration.

details.q: What do the individual dimensions of a dense vector mean?
details.a: Nothing on their own. Only distances and angles between whole vectors carry meaning. That is why you cannot debug a dense retriever by reading dimensions and why sparse signals are still useful for explanation.

details.q: Where do embeddings get computed, and what does that imply for latency?
details.a: Items offline in a batch or stream pipeline, kept in sync on updates; only the query is embedded at request time. Query-time cost is one model call plus one index search, so cache embeddings of frequent queries and keep the query encoder small.

details.q: When should you not use an embedding?
details.a: For exact, auditable decisions: entitlements, compliance, 'block these countries'. A nearest neighbour says 'probably similar', a rule says 'true or false'. Use [user context](#/sd/f/user-context) rules there.

prompts.q: Explain what an item embedding is and why it is useful.
points: Encodes an item as a vector so similarity becomes geometry
Similar meaning means nearby vectors, synonyms land together
Dense learned vectors vs sparse term vectors

prompts.q: Compare dense and sparse representations and say when you would use hybrid.
points: Sparse: exact, interpretable, rare tokens, no synonyms
Query mix with both fuzzy and exact needs
Merge or fuse the two result lists
Cost and complexity of running both

points: Vectors from different models are incompatible
Build a parallel index by re-embedding the corpus offline
Embed queries with the matching version, then cut over
Memory estimate items x dims x bytes, quantization option
Rollback path and recall comparison before the switch
